name: Motion
description: Videos made from HTML: a teaser, a what's-new clip or a walkthrough as a storyboard of scenes, previewed live and rendered to MP4 on this computer. Rendering uses no AI and costs nothing.

tools.description: Make a video in Jig's Motion: a teaser, a what's-new clip or a walkthrough, as a storyboard of scenes the user previews, tweaks and renders to MP4 on their computer (no AI, no cost). Use it when the user asks for a video, teaser, clip, trailer or walkthrough of something; write the scenes yourself from what they gave you (a release, notes, screenshots, the chat). A 40 s teaser is about 6–8 scenes: a title, statements or features, an outro. Returns the video's id; the user sees a card in the chat. Change it later with addon_motion_update, never by making a new one.

kind.description: teaser (short, punchy), whats-new (what changed in a release) or walkthrough (how to do something, with captures)

brief.description: What the video is for and who watches it, in a sentence or two (kept with it; Write with Jig starts from it)

scenes.description: The scenes in order. Each: { id? (only to change an existing scene; keep the ids addon_motion_list shows), type: title | statement | feature | bullets | capture | outro, title, text? (one or two short sentences), bullets? (up to 6 short lines, for a bullets scene), voice? (what the voice says over the scene, also its captions; only when the user wants a voice), duration? (seconds; else timed by reading and voice), media? (path of a screenshot or clip, relative to the chat's folder, for feature and capture scenes) }. A scene shows few words: say it in the voice, not on screen.

language.description: The language of the words, BCP 47 (en, es, sv…); default en

style.description: A style id from addon_motion_list (the project's product kit is `kit` when it has one); default the user's

ownStyle.description: A look of your own instead of `style`: { name, colors: { background, surface?, text, muted?, accent }, fonts?: { headline, body }, radius? }, colours as #hex

settings.description: Video settings to change from the defaults, e.g. { aspect: "9:16" } for a vertical clip, { voice: "af_heart" }, { captions: { on: false } }, { motion: "calm" | "energetic" }

tools.description: Change a Motion video: its scenes (pass the whole list in the new order; scenes keep their media, marks and spoken voice by id unless you change them), title, brief, kind, language, style or settings. Read it first with addon_motion_list and its id.

tools.description: Write a Motion video's own picture as a free composition: your CSS and HTML clips, any layout, any motion, instead of Motion's scene layouts. Use it when the user wants a custom look or motion, or Write with Jig asks for a free composition. Make the video first (addon_motion_create; its scenes are the narration beats: title and voice), then call this with its id; call it again with the whole css and html to change it. Contract: html is what goes inside a frame of the video's size (1920×1080 at 16:9 1080p; addon_motion_list shows the settings). Every part of the picture is a clip: an element with class="clip", data-start and data-duration (seconds in the video) and data-track-index (0, 1, 2…; clips on one track don't overlap; captions use 9). Clips are position:absolute; inset:0 unless your css says otherwise. Put data-scene="s1" on a clip to place that scene's voice and captions there (the voice starts 0.3 s into it; leave the bottom 15% clear for captions). Motion is CSS only: @keyframes with animation-delay counted from the clip's own start, animation-fill-mode both; no transitions on hover, no JavaScript. Use the style's variables: --bg, --surface, --fg, --muted, --accent, --on-accent, --font-headline, --font-body (Inter), --radius, --ease. Images and clips: name files in the chat's folder (src="shots/home.png", copied into the video) or media/… already in it; a <video> needs muted plus its own data-start and data-duration. Not allowed: <script>, <style> (use css), <iframe>, <audio>, forms, on… handlers, http(s) or // URLs, @import. Problems come back as an error to fix. Write for the frame's real pixel size, big type, few words.

seconds.description: The video's length; default where the last clip ends

layouts.description: true to drop the composition and use Motion's scene layouts again

tools.description: Render a Motion video to MP4 (and a poster) on the user's computer: no AI, no cost, a minute or two. Only when the user wants the file; the card in the chat shows progress.

The chat's project's Motion videos (ids, kinds, lengths, whether rendered) and the styles a video can take; with `id`, that video's brief, settings and storyboard, to change it with addon_motion_update.

id.description: A video's id, for its storyboard
